images.title: Four rectangles round a point
images.purpose: Show the example of the concept: 4 rectangles of one size fit round a point with no gap and no overlap, and a 5th would lie over the others.
images.composition: Two panels side by side: on the left four rectangles meeting at a marked point, on the right the same four with a dashed fifth rectangle lying over two of them.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816, scale 36 px for every 1 cm, so every rectangle is 216 by 144 px (6 cm by 4 cm), with a thin dark #2B2B2B outline (4 px). TWO PANELS. LEFT PANEL, centre point at (340, 440): 4 rectangles with one corner each on the point and with their sides meeting edge to edge, forming one block 432 by 288 px: upper right rectangle x 340 to 556, y 296 to 440, teal #0072B2; upper left rectangle x 124 to 340, y 296 to 440, amber #E69F00; lower left rectangle x 124 to 340, y 440 to 584, teal #0072B2; lower right rectangle x 340 to 556, y 440 to 584, amber #E69F00. A reddish purple #CC79A7 dot of 24 px across at the point. At the point, 4 small right angle marks (24 by 24 px squares drawn with a thin dark #2B2B2B outline, no fill), one inside each rectangle at its corner on the point. The text 6 cm (30 px, dark #1F2937) centred above the upper right rectangle at (448, 268) and the text 4 cm centred to the right of the upper right rectangle at (614, 368). RIGHT PANEL, centre point at (1116, 440): the same 4 rectangles and the same dot and right angle marks, with the 4 rectangles at x 900 to 1332 and y 296 to 584 in the same colours, and a 5th rectangle of the same size 216 by 144 px drawn as a DASHED reddish purple #CC79A7 outline (5 px dashes, no fill) with one corner on the point and turned so that its long side points up and to the right: its 4 corners are at (x, y) = (1116, 440), (1269, 287), (1167, 185), (1014, 338). It lies partly over the upper right and the upper left rectangles. The text 5th (36 px, bold, reddish purple) centred inside the dashed rectangle at (1141, 313). PANEL TITLES, bold 44 px dark #1F2937, centred at y 110: 4 rectangles fit at x 340 and A 5th would overlap at x 1116. CAPTIONS, 36 px dark, centred at y 690: no gap and no overlap at x 340 and the 5th lies over the others at x 1116. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any count of rectangles, marks or dots that differs from the numbers stated in the spec, or a gap between the 4 rectangles in the left panel
a dashed rectangle with a solid outline or any fill, or any angle size or other number written at the point
images.takeaway: Shapes fit around a point when their corners fill the space with no gap and no overlap: 4 right angle corners fill it, and a 5th would overlap.
images.description: Four rectangles of one size meeting at a point with no gap, and the same four with a dashed fifth rectangle that overlaps two of them.
images.context: Concept image for Fitting Shapes Around a Point. It follows the idea of the figures in your maths book (shapes placed around a point, with a gap or an overlap) and uses the concept's own rectangles.
images.teaching_notes: Let the child count the four right angle marks at the point and see that they fill the space. The slip to watch: thinking a fifth rectangle can squeeze in.

image_decisions.why: The picture shows 4 rectangles filling the space round a point and a 5th lying over the others.
